For researchers

Research interests

Making power grids with a high share of renewable generation safe, protected and reliable.

  1. Short-circuit behaviour and protection. Short-circuit analysis in grids with a high penetration of inverter-based renewable generation, its influence on conventional protection devices, and how the protection of the grid can be upgraded.
  2. Application: data centers. Data centers are energy-intensive, high-priority loads where voltage dips are costly, so this is where reliable renewable integration matters most.
  3. Policy. Grid connections for new data centers can take five years or more, so approval frameworks may need to change.

Academic experience

MSc thesis, 2025–2026

Impact of Distributed Energy Resources on Short-Circuit Behaviour and Protection Coordination in a Modified CIGRE MV Network: An Adaptive Directional Overcurrent Approach

University of Pavia
Supervisor
Prof. Alessandro Bosisio

Why it matters

Medium-voltage networks were designed for power flowing one way. Solar and CHP units feed fault current from the other direction, and ordinary overcurrent relays start to trip wrongly. I modelled the CIGRE 20 kV benchmark network with eight PV units and one synchronous CHP unit, calculated short circuits to IEC 60909, and designed a protection scheme that copes with it.

Key findings

  • Voltage alone limits the DER hosting window to 31%–172% penetration. I used 150% as the study point.
  • Fault current rises by 9.11% to 19.01% along the DER feeder, highest at the CHP connection bus.
  • Fixed non-directional relays begin to misoperate from 1% penetration and fail at every tested fault location by 136%.
  • A directional element with a maximum torque angle derived from each line's own impedance blocked the reverse current in every fault tested. Backup relays operated at least 0.4213 s after the primary, against a 0.35 s coordination interval.
  • The relay setting group switches at 31% PV penetration over IEC 61850 GOOSE, with a total latency of about 6.1 ms.
  • Cable thermal withstand was verified to IEC 60949. The whole method uses open-source tools (Python, pandapower) and can be reproduced.

Power Electronics course project, March–September 2025

Grid-connected three-phase inverter: design and simulation

University of Pavia
Instructor
Prof. Pericle Zanchetta

Overview

Design an 8 kW inverter for a 230 V grid with an 800 V DC link and 10 kHz switching, then show in simulation that it behaves as designed. Built and tested in PLECS.

Outcome

  • A 5 mH grid inductor keeps the current ripple at 1.33 A, inside the 2 A limit.
  • Simulated inverter voltage is 336.016 V against 336.017 V calculated.
  • The PI current loop, tuned for a damping factor of 0.8 and a 500 Hz natural frequency, follows power steps from zero to half to full power.
  • The DC-link voltage loop, tuned for 0.85 and 10 Hz, brings the DC link to 800 V. At full power the ripple is 0.001 V against a 0.5 V limit.

BSc final-year project, 2021–2022, group project

Centralized control for an islanded DC microgrid

KFUEIT, Rahim Yar Khan
Supervisor
Engr. Dr. Muhammad Umair Shahid

Overview

Three buck converters step 48 V down to a regulated 12 V and supply an LED light, a DC motor and a fan. The converter modules are rated up to about 230 W each.

My contribution

I designed the buck converters with my supervisor's guidance, built the mathematical model and tuned the PID gains for the voltage feedback, ran the MATLAB/Simulink simulations, and wrote the project thesis.

Outcome

The three converter outputs held 11.99 V, 12.06 V and 12.21 V, and load sharing between the converters was achieved.

Milan, Italy

DC power feeds for network equipment in a data center

Facility
Data4, Milan, Italy
Date
19 October 2026, one day
Role
Field engineer

The equipment shelf needed its four power entry modules (PEMs) connected to the rectifier plant. I collected the DC cables, fitted the lugs, and routed them through the horizontal cable conduit inside the rack, between the rectifiers below and the equipment above.

  • Prepared the DC cables with lugs for all four PEMs: blue for −48 V and black for the return.
  • Connected the Rectifier A and Rectifier B breakers, rated 63 A, to the four PEMs. For example, Rectifier B breaker 03 to PEM 3 and breaker 04 to PEM 4.
  • Energised the feeds only after approval from the client's engineer, then checked that PEMs 1, 2, 3 and 4 each showed a green status light and that their fans started.

Junior Electrical Engineer, Lahore Electric Supply Company (LESCO)

Lahore, Pakistan
Field
Grid stations and solar

At LESCO I worked at grid stations during the annual maintenance of power transformers and circuit breakers. I was on site while teams of technicians ran tests such as bushing tests and Buchholz relay testing. I tested transformers under different conditions, recorded the results and reported them, managed the cleaning of SF6 breaker contacts with high-pressure water jets, and helped inspect the control schemes of circuit breakers and magnetic contactors.

In parallel I worked on solarizing government buildings. I surveyed whether solar made sense for each office, sized every PV system from the building's load, oversaw the installation teams against the design and safety standards, and supported the system after installation.
